Admission Arrangements: YR – Y6
Meadhurst Primary School and nursery offer education to children from 2 to 11 years.
Admissions arrangements for all THPT schools comply with the School Admissions Code and the Schools Appeal Code.
THPT adhere to Surrey County Council Local Authority admission procedures which are summarised within the Admissions Criteria.
Our Admissions Policies can be found on our Policies page. Information on Nursery Admissions can be found on our Nursery Admissions Page.
School Appeals Timeline
Appeals for September 2026 entry resulting from year of entry or transfer applications:
Secondary School Admissions
Offer date: 2 March 2026
Primary School Admissions
Please note: Appeals will not start being heard until after the relevant closing date has passed.
Appeals lodged after these dates will be heard within 40 school days of the appeal deadline or 30 school days of being lodged, whichever is the later date.
Appeals are not heard in school holidays, which will vary depending on the school.
Appellants will be sent notification of their appeal hearing at least 10 clear school days in advance of the hearing. Appellants will be sent a copy of the school’s case normally a week in advance of the hearing.
Appellants must ensure that any further evidence not included with their initial appeal is received by the stated deadline, which will be clearly highlighted in the appeal hearing notification letter. Any additional evidence or information received after this date might not be considered at the appeal hearing.
Offer date: 16 April 2026
In year or Immediate Entry Appeals
Appeals resulting from in year admission applications will be heard within 30 school days of the appeal being lodged.

Behaviour
Promoting & Rewarding Good Behaviour and Effort
Rewards are a way that we support the positive reinforcement of behaviour. Public praise and private criticism are adopted within the school. We celebrate achievements as a community. Rewards have a motivational role in helping pupils to realise that good behaviour is valued
Rewards can be given for:
Adults seek to provide specific praise to pupils throughout each day. These are linked to the school rules, values and positive learning behaviours. These behaviours will be recognised through our rewards system
Expectations of Student Conduct
Whilst it is important to reward positive behaviour, it is also important to manage unacceptable or disruptive behaviour in the same positive and consistent manner. Behaviour is a form of communication, and we will make all possible attempts to work with a pupil to understand what they are trying to communicate to others. We have a very clear behaviour grid to outline our procedures for various behaviours and the consequences that will be issued as a result.

Emotional Literacy Support Assistant (ELSA)
An ELSA is a specialist teaching assistant who has received training in emotional literacy support.
ELSA’s are trained by and receive regularly termly supervisions from Educational Psychologists.
An ELSA is a warm, caring and nurturing person who works to help the child feel emotionally supported in school so that they are able to reach their potential educationally and personally.
ELSA support usually runs for 6-8 weeks in a 1:1 session but there are also social groups and wellbeing interventions that have different durations. Additionally, there are wellbeing check ins that can be arranged if appropriate.
We can support with a range of concerns including – Emotional literacy, Regulation, Self Esteem, Positive Relationships, Emotional Regulation and more.

Curriculum Overview
British Values
At Meadhurst School our children learn about the following British Values:
Democracy
The Rule of Law
Individual Liberty
Mutual respect
Tolerance
Anti-Radicalisation
At Meadhurst School, all staff are expected to uphold and promote the fundamental principles of British values. As a school we recognise that safeguarding against radicalisation is no different from safeguarding against any other vulnerability.
Our curriculum promotes respect, tolerance and diversity. Children are encouraged to share their views and recognise that they are entitled to have their own different beliefs which should not be used to influence others.
Our PSHCE (Personal, Social, Health and Citizenship Education), and SMSC (Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural) provision is embedded across the curriculum, and underpins the ethos of the school. It is recognised that children with low aspirations are more vulnerable to radicalisation and therefore we strive to equip our pupils with confidence, self-belief, respect and tolerance as well as setting high standards and expectations for themselves.
Children are regularly taught about how to stay safe when using the Internet and are encouraged to recognise that people are not always who they say they are online. They are taught to seek adult help if they are upset or concerned about anything they read or see on the Internet.

Ordinarily Available Provision (OAP)
SEND
We are committed to equality of opportunity for all pupils.
When concern is expressed regarding a child’s progress, discussion takes place between the parents, the class teacher and a member of the Inclusion team. Diagnostic assessment can be undertaken if required.
If a special need is identified then the child’s name is placed on the Special Needs Register and arrangements made for SEN support. The plan includes targets for improvement, identifies the help required and who will provide it. Progress against the SEN support targets are monitored and parents are kept fully informed.
Therapists, (including speech and language, and occupational therapists) visit the school and provide advice to staff and therapy for those children who have been assessed as requiring additional specialist support.
If you would like to speak to our SENCo then please contact the school office on: 01784 253311 or email: senco@meadhurst.thpt.org.uk.

Attendance
What is Excellent Attendance?
Where appropriate, we will always encourage our children and young people to aim for 100% attendance. However, we appreciate that for some, this is not always possible due to circumstances beyond their control.
Excellent attendance means that a child or young person never misses a day of school without an exceptionally good and authorised reason.
Excellent attendance will look different for different children and young people. Attendance targets should always consider individual needs.
Recognise and celebrate those with 100% attendance
Promoting Good Attendance and Punctuality
All THPT schools will promote a culture of excellent attendance where all stakeholders understand their role in supporting it.
The links between attendance, progress, and attainment will be made clear at every opportunity.
Schools will take a proactive approach to managing attendance. This includes:
To find out more, please view our Attendance Policy on our Policies page.

Home School Link Worker
Family Partnership
Hello, my name is Stephanie Holley, I am the Home School Link Worker & Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead at Meadhurst Primary School.
During term time I work in partnership with parents/carers, schools and other agencies to support families, aiming to reduce current stressful situations and prevent future difficulties.
My aim is to ensure that all children enjoy school and are happy and secure.
Parents/carers, school and children can ask me to become involved. With your consent, we will explore the difficulties your child is experiencing and identify the best way forward.
Should a child protection issue be identified, I am legally bound to follow Government guidelines.
Should you wish to contact me in confidence, please call 01784 253311.
Best wishes, Stephanie
The work I do includes:
Offering support in school,
Supporting parents/carers and families,
Improving attendance and punctuality,
Promoting positive behaviour.
I can help by providing:
One-to-one support, a listening ear and advice
Support groups for parents/carers
Support in accessing Early Help Intervention
Who can I help?

House Teams
Every child from Reception to Year 6 is in a house team.
The four house teams are all precious jewels: Diamond (yellow), Ruby (red), Emerald (green) and Sapphire (blue).
Children are placed in a house upon entering the school. Siblings are taken into account.
Children can earn ‘housepoints’ for good work, being helpful and positive behaviours among other things. Each week the housepoints for the whole school are added up and the winning team is announced in assembly.
House teams are a fantastic opportunity for children to feel part of a team as they each contribute to the totals.
Children will wear house colour t-shirts for PE to help them compete and challenge each other as they learn together.
We have dedicated house captains who organise a range of house competitions each half term to help children value and feel pride in their house team.

Uniform
The uniform is an important part of being a pupil at Meadhurst Primary School. Our expectations of the students’ appearance must remain high at all times. All students are expected to wear the full school uniform, preferably with items that have the school logo, which can be purchased online from our supplier, Primary School Uniforms – School Bells.
Winter Uniform
Teal sweatshirt or cardigan
White polo shirt preferably with school logo
Black knee length skirt or pinafore
Black school trousers
Summer Uniform
Teal sweatshirt or cardigan
White polo shirt preferably with school logo
Black school trousers or Black school shorts
Green gingham summer school dres
Coats
Coats should be named– sportswear such as hoodies and sweat tops are not allowed as coats. A waterproof, reversible logo jacket is available from our Uniform Supplier, Primary School Uniforms – School Bells, this is not compulsory.
Socks & Shoes
Socks should be black in winter and white in summer, either ankle or knee length, or black tights. Trainer socks are not permitted.
School shoes should be sensible, with low heels. Boots, fashion shoes, trainers or strappy sandals are not permitted, even if they are black. Black trainers can be worn for PE and lunchtime activities. Children will be asked to change footwear if it is not appropriate – e.g. plimsoles.
PE Kit
Black shorts
Trainers
A black tracksuit
A black school fleece is available
Bags
Each pupil is required to have a PE kit bag and either a book bag or ruck sack ( depending on the year group your child is in).
Reception – Yr 2 pupils use Book Bags or rucksack.
Yr 3 – Yr 6 pupils use a rucksack.
These bags are available through our uniform supplier, Primary School Uniforms – School Bells
